proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (shells W_j = T⌞S_j, D_j = (∂T)⌞S_j with S_0 = {d ≥ r_0}, S_{j+1} = {r_{j+1} ≤ d < r_j}, items (a)–(d)) together with the identity ∂A_t = B_t + P_t of step 4. Dependency: im_restrict. Notation: M = RT.carrier, θ = RT.mult, ξ = RT.orient, M′ = RB.carrier, θ′ = RB.mult, ξ′ = RB.orient; for ω ∈ 𝒟^m put g_ω(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)((dω)(x)) (dω = exteriorDerivative ω) and h_ω(x) := θ′(x)ξ′(x)(ω(x)); for η ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} put k_η(x) := θ(x)ξ(x)(η(x)).
1. ∂T vanishes off K: if tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂T(ω) = T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω) = 0; the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω is exteriorDerivative ω by definition.
2. Integrability: by im_restrict (A) for RT and RB, g_ω and k_η are integrable on M and h_ω on M′ (dω is a test form by exteriorDerivative_isTestForm).
3. Representations: T(η) = ∫_M k_η (RT represents T); hence ∂T(ω) = T(dω) = ∫_M g_ω; and ∂T(ω) = ∫_{M′} h_ω (RB represents ∂T).
4. Splitting (integral_inter_add_sdiff with the measurable sets {a ≤ f} and {f < b}; f is continuous, hence measurable): for G ∈ {M, M′}, u integrable on G and reals b ≤ a: (i) ∫_G u = ∫_{G∩{a≤f}} u + ∫_{G∩{f<a}} u, because G ∖ {a ≤ f} = G ∩ {f < a}; (ii) ∫_{G∩{f<a}} u = ∫_{G∩{f<b}} u + ∫_{G∩{b≤f<a}} u, because (G ∩ {f < a}) ∩ {f < b} = G ∩ {f < b} (as b ≤ a) and (G ∩ {f < a}) ∖ {f < b} = G ∩ {b ≤ f ∧ f < a}.
5. Construction (im_restrict (B)): with X = T, R = RT and F = K, let W_0 be the restriction to {r_0 ≤ f}, W_{j+1} the restriction to {r_{j+1} ≤ f ∧ f < r_j}, A_N the restriction to {f < r_N}; with X = ∂T, R = RB and F = K (allowed by step 1), let D_0 be the restriction to {r_0 ≤ f} and D_{j+1} the restriction to {r_{j+1} ≤ f ∧ f < r_j}. All these sets are measurable. Define W and D on ℕ by cases (W 0 = W_0, W (j+1) = W_{j+1}; likewise D). im_restrict gives: each W_j, D_j is IM; the integral formulas (e.g. W_0(η) = ∫_{M∩{r_0≤f}} k_η, D_0(ω) = ∫_{M′∩{r_0≤f}} h_ω, A_N(η) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_N}} k_η); the masses M(W_0) = μ_RT({r_0 ≤ f}), M(W_{j+1}) = μ_RT({r_{j+1} ≤ f < r_j}), M(D_0) = μ_RB({r_0 ≤ f}), M(D_{j+1}) = μ_RB({r_{j+1} ≤ f < r_j}), M(A_N) = μ_RT({f < r_N}); and each vanishes off K ∩ B for its set B.
6. Vanishing of W_j and D_j off E_j: for j = 0, K ∩ {r_0 ≤ f} = E_0; for j + 1, K ∩ {r_{j+1} ≤ f ∧ f < r_j} ⊆ E_{j+1}, so disjointness from E_{j+1} implies disjointness from that set (Disjoint.mono_right).
7. Boundary of W_0: ∂W_0(ω) = W_0(dω) = ∫_{M∩{r_0≤f}} g_ω = ∫_M g_ω − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω (4(i)) = ∂T(ω) − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω (step 3). Also D_0(ω) = ∫_{M′∩{r_0≤f}} h_ω = ∂T(ω) − ∫_{M′∩{f<r_0}} h_ω (4(i), step 3) and Z_0(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω − ∫_{M′∩{f<r_0}} h_ω (hypothesis). Therefore D_0(ω) − Z_0(ω) = ∂T(ω) − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} g_ω = ∂W_0(ω).
8. Boundary of W_{j+1}: r_{j+1} ≤ r_j (r antitone), so by 4(ii) ∂W_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{M∩{r_{j+1}≤f<r_j}} g_ω = ∫_{M∩{f<r_j}} g_ω − ∫_{M∩{f<r_{j+1}}} g_ω and D_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{M′∩{f<r_j}} h_ω − ∫_{M′∩{f<r_{j+1}}} h_ω. With the formulas for Z_j(ω) and Z_{j+1}(ω), D_{j+1}(ω) + Z_j(ω) − Z_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_j}} g_ω − ∫_{M∩{f<r_{j+1}}} g_ω = ∂W_{j+1}(ω).
9. Partial sums, by induction on N: Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j(η) = T(η) − A_N(η). For N = 0: W_0(η) = ∫_{M∩{r_0≤f}} k_η = ∫_M k_η − ∫_{M∩{f<r_0}} k_η = T(η) − A_0(η). For N → N + 1: Σ_{j≤N+1} W_j(η) = T(η) − A_N(η) + W_{N+1}(η) (Finset.sum_range_succ), and A_N(η) = ∫_{M∩{f<r_N}} k_η = ∫_{M∩{f<r_{N+1}}} k_η + ∫_{M∩{r_{N+1}≤f<r_N}} k_η = A_{N+1}(η) + W_{N+1}(η) by 4(ii).
10. Vanishing of Z_j off E_j, by induction on j; note E_j ⊆ E_{j+1} since r is antitone. If tsupport ω ∩ E_0 = ∅, then by step 7 Z_0(ω) = D_0(ω) − ∂W_0(ω), where D_0(ω) = 0 (step 6) and ∂W_0(ω) = W_0(dω) = 0 because tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (step 6). If the claim holds for j and tsupport ω ∩ E_{j+1} = ∅, then by step 8 Z_{j+1}(ω) = D_{j+1}(ω) + Z_j(ω) − ∂W_{j+1}(ω) with D_{j+1}(ω) = 0, ∂W_{j+1}(ω) = W_{j+1}(dω) = 0 (step 6) and Z_j(ω) = 0 (induction hypothesis, since tsupport ω is disjoint from E_j ⊆ E_{j+1}).
11. Steps 5–10 give all conclusions. ∎
key_steps: ∂T vanishes off K; all integrands are integrable (im_restrict (A)).
Shells, ∂T-shells and the sublevel pieces A_N are IM restrictions (im_restrict (B)) with the stated masses and vanishing sets.
Integral splitting along {f < r_j} gives ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0, ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} + Z_j − Z_{j+1} and Σ_{j≤N} W_j = T − A_N.
Induction on j shows Z_j vanishes off E_j using these relations and E_j ⊆ E_{j+1}.
